data.name: pictureBox7.ToolTip
data.value: A log layout contains the definition of what each log line looks like. This includes: - the date-time expected at the start of each line (stack traces without a date are allowed). - the metadata written per log line, which can be filtered on. - content data that can be quickly navigated to and which can be colored in the log

data.name: pictureBox13.ToolTip
data.value:
Automatically detects the timestamp at the start of each log line. If automatic detection does not work, disable it and specify a custom datetime format.
d: Represents the day of the month as a number from 1 through 31. dd: Represents the day of the month as a number from 01 through 31. ddd: Represents the abbreviated name of the day (Mon, Tues, Wed, etc). dddd: Represents the full name of the day (Monday, Tuesday, etc). h: 12-hour clock hour (e.g. 4). hh: 12-hour clock, with a leading 0 (e.g. 06) H: 24-hour clock hour (e.g. 15) HH: 24-hour clock hour, with a leading 0 (e.g. 22) m: Minutes mm: Minutes with a leading zero M: Month number(eg.3) MM: Month number with leading zero(eg.04) MMM: Abbreviated Month Name (e.g. Dec) MMMM: Full month name (e.g. December) s: Seconds ss: Seconds with leading zero t: Abbreviated AM / PM (e.g. A or P) tt: AM / PM (e.g. AM or PM y: Year, no leading zero (e.g. 2015 would be 15) yy: Year, leading zero (e.g. 2015 would be 015) yyy: Year, (e.g. 2015) yyyy: Year, (e.g. 2015) K: Represents the time zone information of a date and time value (e.g. +05:00) z: With DateTime values represent the signed offset of the local operating system's time zone from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), measured in hours. (e.g. +6) zz: As z, but with leading zero (e.g. +06) zzz: With DateTime values represents the signed offset of the local operating system's time zone from UTC, measured in hours and minutes. (e.g. +06:00) f: Represents the most significant digit of the seconds fraction; that is, it represents the tenths of a second in a date and time value. ff: Represents the two most significant digits of the second's fraction in date and time fff: Represents the three most significant digits of the second's fraction; that is, it represents the milliseconds in a date and time value. ffff: Represents the four most significant digits of the second's fraction; that is, it represents the ten-thousandths of a second in a date and time value. While it is possible to display the ten thousandths of a second component of a time value, that value may not be meaningful. fffff: Represents the five most significant digits of the second's fraction; that is, it represents the hundred-thousandths of a second in a date and time value. ffffff: Represents the six most significant digits of the second's fraction; that is, it represents the millionths of a second in a date and time value. fffffff: Represents the seven most significant digits of the second's fraction; that is, it represents the ten-millionths of a second in a date and time value.

data.name: pictureBox11.ToolTip
data.value:
Specify the text that identifies the end of the metadata and the start of the actual log line content.
For example 2025-01-01T01:02:03.123 INFO metadataA=ValueX, MetadataB=ValueY - Example log line text Use in this example: " -"
The application uses this information, among other things, to remove the metadata and show a more readable log
If the Regex option is checked, the metadata text matching the Regex expression is searched for, the text after the metadata is considered content. Do not use ^ at the start of the Regex. The regex searches after the timestamp, so that does not need to be in the regex.
Use the following regex to search for multiple spaces from the timestamp, for example 8: (?:\s+\S+){8}

data.name: pictureBox18.ToolTip
data.value:
If this option is enabled and the specified content is found, the corresponding log line is marked as an error.
These errors are counted and reported, and within the content filters, errors are displayed separately in red among the other content (this is configurable).

data.name: pictureBox17.ToolTip
data.value:
It is possible to show a hierarchical view of log lines that describe a flow and any sub-flows. Select this option if this content filter marks the start of a (sub)flow. Then select in the dropdown the content filter that indicates the corresponding end of the (sub)flow.
The application uses this to recognize the starts and ends of indicated flows and how they are nested within each other. This is converted into a hierarchical view.
Once this option is enabled, the selected content filter can be displayed hierarchically.
Note: If the hierarchical view is very large or (partially) incorrect, the log file may need to be filtered further. Limit the log to the session you are interested in to avoid noise.

data.name: pictureBox9.ToolTip
data.value:
Specify the text that appears right before the content value and (optionally) the text that appears right after the content value. Put between the before and after text: => It is possible to specify multiple before and after texts, put each on its own line.
Example: if the log line contains API call: X Then specify: API call:
Example: if the log line contains API call: X is being started Then specify: API call: => is being started

data.name: pictureBox6.ToolTip
data.value:
Specify filters here for the content of log lines. By searching for a specific text or word combination, you can quickly navigate to relevant log lines. The corresponding navigation is displayed on the right side of the screen.
In addition, a color coding can be set for each filter, so log lines are automatically displayed in color.
A filter can consist of just the text before the desired value, or of both the text before and after the value. When both are specified, they must be separated with =>. The text between these two parts is considered the value and is displayed in the navigation.
Example: 2025-01-01 01:02:03.123 INFO MetadataX=ValueY - Example log text and here starts the API call: X
To find the value X, API call: can be specified as the filter. The text after the value does not need to be filled in then.
When both a start and end text are known, for example API call: => end can be specified. In that case, the text between API call: and end is used as the value and displayed in the navigation.

data.name: pictureBox2.ToolTip
data.value:
A date time is always expected at the start of the log line. Make sure the format matches how it appears in the log line.
Specifier Example Meaning yyyy 2025 Full year (4 digits) yy 25 Year in 2 digits MM 04 Month (with leading zero) M 4 Month (without leading zero) dd 14 Day of the month (with zero) d 14 Day of the month (without zero) dddd Monday Full name of the day ddd Mon Abbreviated day name
HH 09 Hour (24-hour, with zero) H 9 Hour (24-hour, without zero) hh 09 Hour (12-hour, with zero) h 9 Hour (12-hour, without zero) mm 07 Minutes (with zero) m 7 Minutes (without zero) ss 04 Seconds (with zero) s 4 Seconds (without zero) tt AM / PM Morning / afternoon
fff 123 Milliseconds zz +02 Time zone offset in hours zzz +02:00 Time zone offset with minutes
Examples yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss 2025-04-14 13:45:30 Full date + time (24-hour) yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss 2025-04-14T13:45:30 ISO 8601 notation (e.g. for JSON) ddd dd MMM yyyy Mon 14 Apr 2025 Readable date, abbreviated day/month dddd dd MMMM yyyy Monday 14 April 2025 Fully spelled out date yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff 2025-04-14 13:45:30.123 Including milliseconds yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss zzz 2025-04-14 13:45:30 +02:00 With time zone offset
